page.layout: One block of running text at the top of the page, ending with a date line and its numeral line; below it a large woodcut ornament (decorative fleuron, no text). No margin notes, no running head, no page number.

main_text.p: liabitur, ille & iste in suâ caussâ. Interea CRVCEM accipite, atque etiam ferte. Vt columna, quæ recta stat, impositò magis pondere firmatur: sic altas rectásque mentes oportet, non cedere oneri, sed obniti. Vos per vos facietis, ita vterque ille faueat & auxilietur, quem dixi. Louanij, pridie Nonas Nouemb.

page.notes: The ornament below the text is a woodcut fleuron and is not transcribed. The printed date line reads "∞. IO. XCII." as printed, where ∞ is an old symbol for the thousands mark. The text "Vos per vos facietis.ita vterque" has a full stop as printed before "ita". Some early letters are worn at the top-left edge of the scan ("liabitur" begins a fragment of a previous line; the first letter is likely "h" or "l" and is printed as "liabitur" in the scan).
